subject: Sole remedy / SLA credit trigger & evidence — Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Rachel Burns <rachel.burns@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@clearwaterhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form redlines — sole remedy / credits question

Karthik,

Thanks for the draft Order Form — attaching our redlines (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). A couple of items our GC flagged that we need clarification on before we can move to signature:

- The MSA currently says service credits are the 'sole and exclusive remedy' for downtime. Our counsel is asking whether that language would bar recoveries for data loss, IP infringement, or willful misconduct.
- Do service credits reduce the liability cap (i.e., are credits offset against damages)? If so, what is the order of operations?
- What evidence do you require from us to trigger credits? We need an operational list (ticket IDs, logs, timestamps) we can present to our compliance team.

We would like a short call to align on an approach that protects both sides. Proposed times next week.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Burns
Director, IT Procurement
Clearwater Health Inc.

Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order Form redlines — sole remedy / credits question

Looping legal and product in — see Clearwater's redlines. High-level view and suggested options below; please weigh in with drafting and operational feasibility.

Summary of their concerns: credits as sole remedy; credits potentially reducing the liability cap; and what constitutes adequate evidence.

Commercial options to consider (quick framing):
A) 'Credits are the sole remedy for service availability; credits do not reduce or count toward the liability cap; carve-outs for confidentiality, IP/infringement, gross negligence, willful misconduct remain.' (This is customer-friendly, increases our exposure.)
B) 'Credits are the sole remedy for availability and will be offset against any recoverable damages but cannot reduce the cap below zero; explicit credits cap (e.g., 3x monthly fees) sits behind the liability cap.' (Middle ground.)
C) 'Keep current language: credits sole remedy and reduce cap — faster to close but likely a negotiation blocker.)

Operational asks for product/ops: if we require evidence, can we commit to an evidence checklist: ticket ID + start/end timestamps + support transcript + internal metrics snapshot? What retention window for logs can we provide? Dev, can you attach SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx and confirm feasibility?

Target: I'd like a recommended legal position + redline by next Friday (2027-05-07) so we can schedule a call with Clearwater the following week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — sole remedy / credits question

Karthik — thanks, reading now. High‑level legal/commercial take: we should avoid an absolute 'credits do not reduce cap' for deals where the customer is price-sensitive unless Commercial is comfortable adding a small premium. That said, I think we can land a defensible drafting approach that balances risk and sale velocity.

Suggested path:
1) Narrow the 'sole remedy' scope so it references only 'Service Unavailability' as defined in the SLA; explicitly carve out the following from the sole remedy limitation: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) misappropriation or IP infringement; (c) gross negligence or willful misconduct; (d) indemnified claims.
2) Adopt a clear order of operations clause: Service Credits are payable pursuant to the SLA and are not themselves 'damages' but will be applied as an offset against recoverable amounts up to a separate 'credits cap'. The liability cap remains intact — but specify whether credits count towards the cap or sit outside of it.

Draft language suggestion (for discussion):
'Except as expressly set forth in this section, Service Credits are the sole and exclusive contractual remedy for Service Unavailability. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section shall not limit Customer's rights for breaches arising from confidentiality obligations, willful misconduct, fraud, or infringement of Customer's intellectual property, nor shall it limit amounts payable under indemnity provisions.'

Audit process we should include in the Order Form (operational):
- Customer must submit a ticket within 14 days of alleged downtime with incident start/end times and ticket ID.
- Redwood will provide evidence from system logs (request sample window — default 90 days retention) and validate within 10 business days.
- If disagreement persists, parties agree to escalation to a joint review call and an independent log snapshot review.

I'll add specific redline snippets to OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf and attach it after review.

Laura
VP, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — legal analysis and proposed clauses

Thanks — legal analysis below. I prefer a calibrated approach that preserves a commercially viable cap while protecting customers on sensitive categories. Key points:

- Carve-outs from the limitation of liability should be explicit: (i) breach of confidentiality / unauthorized data access; (ii) willful misconduct; (iii) IP infringement; (iv) bodily injury or death (if applicable, likely not in our SaaS context); (v) indemnity obligations.
- On credits vs cap: recommended hybrid language: 'Service Credits shall be payable as set forth in the SLA. Service Credits shall not be treated as damages for purposes of calculating the Parties' aggregate liability, provided that in the event Customer recovers an award or settlement that includes both Service Credits and other compensatory damages, the amount of Service Credits shall be credited against such award up to the aggregate Service Credit cap.' In short: credits are generally not damages but will be credited back against any award to avoid double recovery.
- Evidence standard: require customer to provide ticket ID, earliest notification time, and attach the Redwood support transcript. Failure to provide these within 14 days forfeits credit entitlement. We should keep the default log retention note at 90 days.
- Proposed redline for Order Form: include a 'Service Credit Process' exhibit that lists required artifacts and timelines, and an 'Escalation & Audit' paragraph that allows Redwood to produce internal metrics and a single independent snapshot if disputed.

Commercial impact: removing credit offset entirely increases potential exposure; if Sales wants 'credits outside cap', Commercial should price for it. If not, hybrid will protect both sides and is defensible in negotiation.

I'll prepare a redline for signature that reflects the hybrid.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Watson <tom.watson@clearwaterhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Burns <rachel.burns@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@clearwaterhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — sole remedy / credits question

Karthik / team — appreciate the rapid turnaround. Clearwater is open to a compromise along Neha's hybrid lines but we have two asks:
1) Any offsets of credits against awards should be limited to credits that were actually paid (not credits merely accrued).
2) Clear evidence checklist up front. We are prepared to submit ticket IDs and support threads; we also need a machine‑readable export of the event timestamps (we have attached a sample Downtime-logs-sample.txt).

If Redwood's position is that credits can be credited back against recoveries only if paid, we can accept the hybrid language and the carve-outs for confidentiality/IP/willful misconduct. We think a 14‑day submission window + 90‑day log retention is fair.

Can we schedule a 30‑minute alignment call Thursday 2027‑05‑06 to finalize?

Tom Watson
Sr. Counsel, Clearwater Health Inc.

Attachment: Downtime-logs-sample.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — next steps and decision framing

Thanks everyone — useful discussion. Quick summary and proposed next steps so we can close the Order Form: 

Decision framing: Redwood is willing to adopt the hybrid approach Neha proposed with the following concrete drafting points: 
- Service Credits will be payable per the SLA and are not deemed "damages" for calculation of the aggregate liability cap, but to prevent double recovery, credits actually paid may be credited against any monetary award for the same incident up to the Service Credit cap.
- The sole remedy language will be narrowed to 'Service Unavailability' and explicitly carve out confidentiality breaches, willful misconduct, IP infringement, and indemnity claims.
- Evidence: Customer must submit a support ticket within 14 days with ticket ID, start/end timestamps, and conversational transcript; Redwood will provide a log snapshot (default retention 90 days). Disputes escalate to a joint review within 10 business days.

Operational asks: Dev, confirm we can provide machine‑readable timestamp exports and honor the 90‑day retention and the 10 business day validation SLA. Laura/Neha, please prepare final redline and incorporate the 'Service Credit Process' exhibit.

If legal and product can sign off, I'll propose a short call with Clearwater to finalize on 2027‑05‑06 and then move the Order Form to DocuSign. I've dropped a preliminary DocuSign link below for reference — will populate when redlines are final.

Next steps: 
- Legal to circulate final redline by EOD 2027‑05‑04.
- Dev to confirm log export format and retention by 2027‑05‑04.
- Schedule call with Clearwater for 2027‑05‑06 (Karthik to send invite).
